title: Symptom record text quotes the UTC instant beside a local zone name
trigger: User in America/Chicago saves a symptom observed 2026-09-11 21:15 local; SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:40 writes observedAt via RevaDate.iso (always 'Z'), so observedAt = 2026-09-12T02:15:00Z, timeZone = America/Chicago; recordText line 66 renders the pair verbatim.
expected: The record body (quoted source for reports, visible record text) states the occurrence in the user's zone or with its real offset, agreeing with the record's list date.
actual: Record text reads 'Occurred at: 2026-09-12T02:15:00Z (America/Chicago)' while record.date is '2026-09-11' (derived in the entry zone, SymptomEntry.swift:101-107). Tests/RevaCoreTests/SymptomEntryTests.swift:77 pins the text and :88 pins the list date, so the mismatch is the current contract. Browser twin apps/web/src/core/symptoms.ts:57 is identical.
impact: Report quotations copy the line verbatim; a reader can attribute the symptom to the wrong day, and the zone suffix invites reading 02:15 as local time. No data loss (observedAt/timeZone stored precisely in symptomEntry).
evidence: sed -n '63,67p;101,107p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/SymptomEntry.swift; sed -n '40p' apps/ios/Reva/Features/Records/SymptomEntryEditorView.swift; sed -n '77p;88p' Tests/RevaCoreTests/SymptomEntryTests.swift; evidence/r1-10-swift-test-root.log lines 104-118 (SymptomEntryTests pass as written).
smallestFix: In recordText format observedAt in entry.timeZone with an explicit offset (e.g. '2026-09-11 21:15 (America/Chicago, UTC-05:00)'); mirror in apps/web/src/core/symptoms.ts:57; update the pinned test strings in both clients in the same change.
regressionCheck: SymptomEntryTests: entry 2026-09-12T02:15:00Z / America/Chicago yields record text containing '2026-09-11' and '21:15'; browser symptoms test asserts the identical string.
ownerTrack: Person 1 (records); Captain for the browser twin

title: 1800-character excerpt cut can split a value, unit or negation with no marker
trigger: A record page whose first 24 non-blank content lines join to more than 1800 characters (e.g. an OCR'd lab table of 24 lines x ~80 chars). localExcerpt (line 15) is stored as the summary after each text edit (RecordEditorView.swift:65-67) and is the report quotation for pages without a focus hit; relevantExcerpt applies the same cut at line 165.
expected: Quotations end at a line boundary or carry a visible marker so 'Potassium 4.15 mmol/L' cannot become 'Potassium 4.1' and 'No chest pain' cannot become 'No'.
actual: .prefix(1800) cuts at an arbitrary character with no ellipsis or boundary logic. DomainTests.swift:114-117 checks negation only on a 3-line text; FixtureEvidenceTests.swift:136-138 and DomainTests.swift:165 ground excerpts by substring containment, which a mid-token cut still satisfies. Browser twin apps/web/src/core/domain.ts:61,161 has the same cut.
impact: Altered dose/unit/negation in the 'Local excerpt' summary and in the pre-visit brief for long pages. Not exercised by the checked-in seed (max joined length 888 chars).
evidence: sed -n '14,16p;161,165p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/ReportEngine.swift; scratchpad port_check.out section 5 (seed max 888); ER-02-02 item 4 requests the Swift demonstration.
smallestFix: Cut at the last newline (or whitespace) at or before 1800 and append a marker such as ' [...]' in the excerpt only (not in signature inputs), in localExcerpt and relevantExcerpt and their browser twins.
regressionCheck: Unit test: 24 lines x 80 chars ending 'Potassium 4.15 mmol/L' -> excerpt ends at a line boundary, contains no partial token, still passes the grounded-substring assertion.

title: Page tie-break selects the last page for zero-hit or tied multi-page records
trigger: Multi-page record selected by pin (score 1000) or context tag whose pages score equally for the visit focus (seed: 2-page demo-record-tibia-procedure under demo-visit-primary-20260908 scores [1,1]; any pinned scan with zero hits scores all 0).
expected: With no distinguishing hit the citation points at page 1 (the document opening, which is what the fallback excerpt quotes), or the tie rule is explicit and tested.
actual: Sequence.max(by:) replaces the running maximum whenever areInIncreasingOrder(current, candidate) is true; the closure returns lhs.offset < rhs.offset on ties, so a later page always wins and the reference cites the last page. The excerpt is that page's opening lines, so the citation is grounded but points at the least informative page for scans ending in signature/footer pages. Browser twin domain.ts:180-183 uses 'score >= maximum' (same last-page result).
impact: Lower-quality citations for pinned/context documents; no false quotation.
evidence: sed -n '112,118p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/ReportEngine.swift; sed -n '180,183p' apps/web/src/core/domain.ts; port_check.out section 4 ([(1,0),(1,0)] tie under the completed visit); Swift Sequence.max(by:) semantics.
smallestFix: Return lhs.offset > rhs.offset on ties (first page wins) in Swift and use 'score > maximum' in the browser; add a comment stating the rule.
regressionCheck: Unit test: 3-page record with zero focus hits and a pin cites page 1; 2-page record with hits only on page 2 still cites page 2.

title: Generic goal words become relevance terms and the fixture trailer is indexed
trigger: Completed seed visit demo-visit-primary-20260908 (concern 'Discuss patient-reported brief palpitations and nausea.', goal 'Review existing source documents and organize unresolved questions before the follow-up visit.').
expected: The unrelated ear note is excluded for a palpitations/nausea visit (E02), or at least not selected on document-generic words.
actual: 'patient', 'reported', 'documents', 'existing', 'organize' pass the >3-letter/stop-word filter (line 72) and the index (lines 77-79) is built from the full text including the demo trailer sentences, so every seed record matches; the ear record scores 30 and all nine records are selected. No expected-evidence scenario exists for this visit, so no test constrains it.
impact: Over-inclusion for goals written in everyday language; not a false citation.
evidence: sed -n '68,72p;77,79p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/ReportEngine.swift; port_check.out section 2 (ear-infection 30 via documents/patient/reported); ER-02-02 item 2 requests Swift confirmation.
smallestFix: Extend the stop list with document-generic words (patient, reported, documents, existing, organize, unresolved) and build the index from contentLines(record.text) so the fixture trailer is not indexed; add an expected-evidence scenario for the completed visit.
regressionCheck: FixtureEvidenceTests scenario for demo-visit-primary-20260908 with mustExclude demo-record-ear-infection passes.

title: Fixture-wrapper stripping is applied to every user document
trigger: A real uploaded document whose first 10 non-blank lines contain a line starting 'Source date:' or 'Week ending:', or any line starting 'Invented for Reva software demonstration.'.
expected: Excerpts of user documents quote from the first line; only demo fixtures carry the wrapper.
actual: contentLines drops everything up to and including the last such metadata line among the first 10 lines and everything from the trailer line on, for all records (no isDemo check, Models.swift:40 flag unused). A lab report headed 'Source date: 2026-09-01' loses its heading block from the summary/quotation and from page scoring (which also uses contentLines).
impact: Missing header context in excerpts; record.text is intact so nothing is lost from storage.
smallestFix: Apply the marker stripping only when record.isDemo (pass the flag to contentLines/localExcerpt), or move the wrapper out of fixture text.
regressionCheck: Unit test: non-demo record starting 'Source date: 2026-09-01\nPotassium 4.1 mmol/L' keeps both lines in localExcerpt.

title: RevaDate.display(time: false) renders the UTC calendar day of instants
trigger: A report generated at 21:30 America/Chicago on 2026-09-11 has createdAt = 2026-09-12T02:30:00Z; ReportView.swift:27 shows RevaDate.display(report.createdAt); RecordingDetailView.swift:27 does the same for recording.createdAt.
expected: 'Prepared Sep 11, 2026' (the user's day), consistent with the comment on Models.swift:203 ('display actual instants in the supplied zone').
actual: display uses TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0) whenever time == false, so the header reads 'Prepared Sep 12, 2026'. Correct for date-only values (record dates) but the callers pass instants. Browser formatDate has the same UTC rule (domain.ts:28).
impact: Off-by-one day labels for evening activity west of UTC; cosmetic but medical-context sensitive.
evidence: sed -n '203p;225,231p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/Models.swift; sed -n '27p' apps/ios/Reva/Features/Preparation/ReportView.swift; sed -n '27p' apps/ios/Reva/Features/Visits/RecordingDetailView.swift; sed -n '28p' apps/web/src/core/domain.ts.
smallestFix: Callers that display instants pass time: true (or add a dayOfInstant(zone:) variant); mirror in the browser formatDate callers.
regressionCheck: Unit test: RevaDate.display('2026-09-12T02:30:00Z', time: true, zone: 'America/Chicago') contains 'Sep 11'.

title: Visit ordering compares ISO strings lexically; mixed offsets misorder same-day visits
trigger: Seed visits carry '-05:00' offsets (2026-09-15T09:00:00-05:00 = 14:00Z); app-created visits use RevaDate.iso ('Z'). A visit created for 2026-09-15 13:00Z sorts after the 14:00Z seed visit because '...T13:00:00Z' > '...T09:00:00-05:00' lexically. BookingEngine.confirm (BookingEngine.swift:31) copies request.earliest verbatim.
expected: Visits ordered by instant (records already sort via RevaDate.parse, AppStore.swift:91-96).
actual: var visits sorts with $0.date < $1.date (string comparison); Visit.date is an unnormalized String (Models.swift:105).
impact: Wrong order in the visits list when formats mix (imports, browser-created data, demo seed plus user visits). Outside this track's strict scope (AppStore is track 03/04); the model contract is in scope.
evidence: sed -n '91,98p' apps/ios/Reva/State/AppStore.swift; sed -n '105,106p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/Models.swift; sed -n '31p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/BookingEngine.swift; demo/seed.json visit dates.
smallestFix: Sort by RevaDate.parse($0.date) with id tie-break, or normalize Visit.date to UTC 'Z' on save.
regressionCheck: Unit test: sorting visits dated ['2026-09-15T13:00:00Z', '2026-09-15T09:00:00-05:00'] yields the 'Z' visit first.

title: Visit has no version; save(visit) is whole-value replace (last writer wins)
trigger: Visit editor open while a pull completes or an AI report lands; the editor's save replaces the stored visit (lines 16-17).
expected: E01: concurrent edits do not overwrite each other; records already guard on version (AppStore+Records.swift:20-24, AppStore+Symptoms.swift:23).
actual: Visit (Models.swift:99-114) has no version/updatedAt; save is unconditional replace. The AI path is protected by its signature re-check (AppStore+AI.swift:51) but the plain editor save is not.
impact: Stale editor copy can discard a pulled report/notes/questions. Secondary path; suggestion because it needs a model addition.
smallestFix: Add an optional version/updatedAt to Visit (nil default for legacy decode) and reject stale saves as records do.
regressionCheck: Test: save(visit) with an outdated copy throws after the stored visit changed.

title: BookingEngine.validate accepts unparsable date strings
trigger: BookingRequest with earliest 'abc' and latest 'xyz' (only reachable via imported/synced data; native editors write RevaDate.iso).
expected: validate rejects requests whose window does not parse.
actual: RevaDate.parse returns .distantPast for unparsable text, so distantPast <= distantPast passes; confirm later writes visit.date = 'abc' (line 31). testBookingConfirmationIsIdempotentAndBounded covers idempotency/bounds, not rejection of malformed dates, short phone, bad zone or non-proposed status.
impact: Malformed visit date can be written on a secondary path.
smallestFix: Require both dates to parse (strict parser or != .distantPast) and add failure-path tests.
regressionCheck: Tests: validate throws for unparsable earliest/latest, 9-digit phone, invalid zone; confirm throws for status != proposed.

title: Per-call formatter allocation in RevaDate and per-access sorting/hashing (unmeasured)
trigger: Any SwiftUI body evaluation that reads store.records or renders the visits list.
actual: parse allocates up to three formatters per call; AppStore.records sorts on every access with two parse calls per comparison (O(N log N) parses per evaluation); isStale hashes the full record corpus per visit row (VisitsView.swift:45). Asymptotic argument only; no measurement exists, so this is not a defect claim.
impact: Plausible UI latency at the server's 5000-record cap; unknown at demo scale.
evidence: sed -n '204,216p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/Models.swift; sed -n '91,98p' apps/ios/Reva/State/AppStore.swift; sed -n '45p' apps/ios/Reva/Features/Preparation/VisitsView.swift; ER-02-02 item 5 requests a bounded timing.
smallestFix: Cache formatters as static lets (ISO8601DateFormatter is thread-safe) and memoize sorted arrays/signatures per snapshot revision after measuring.
regressionCheck: Timing from ER-02-02 before/after; existing tests unchanged.

title: VisitReport.isDemo defaults to true for locally generated reports
trigger: ReportEngine.generate builds a VisitReport without setting isDemo; only the AI path sets it false (AppStore+AI.swift:68).
expected: Reports over real user records are not flagged as demo data.
actual: Every local report is serialized with isDemo = true to the server and browser. Nothing native reads the flag today.
impact: A future demo badge or cleanup filter would misclassify real reports.
evidence: sed -n '87,98p' apps/ios/Reva/Core/Models.swift; sed -n '66,68p' apps/ios/Reva/State/AppStore+AI.swift; ReportEngine.swift:140-147 (no isDemo argument).
smallestFix: Default isDemo to false and set true only for seeded demo reports, or drop the flag.
regressionCheck: Test: ReportEngine.generate over a non-demo record yields report.isDemo == false.

title: Test gaps: Swift signature goldens, page ties, truncation boundary, booking rejections, RevaDate zones, legacy snapshot shape
trigger: Reading all seven files in Tests/RevaCoreTests.
expected: Tests assert the literal signature goldens shared with the browser, page selection on ties/zero hits, the 1800-char cut, BookingEngine rejection paths, RevaDate.display/day zone behavior, decoding of a first-commit-shaped snapshot, and a DST-crossing visit.
actual: None of those exist; legacy tests only remove optional keys (SymptomEntryTests.swift:122-125, MedicalProfileTests.swift:13-17). Existing tests do assert user outcomes (staleness, pins, grounded citations, question authority, list date) and several failure paths.
impact: Regressions in E03/E04 parity or date handling would not be caught natively.
evidence: Tests/RevaCoreTests/*.swift read in full; evidence/r1-10-swift-test-root.log (44 tests, 0 failures); apps/web/src/core/__tests__/domain.test.ts:20-26 (browser holds the goldens).
smallestFix: Add the listed tests; the golden test decodes demo/seed.json and compares ReportEngine.signature to the three hex strings in domain.test.ts:24-26.
regressionCheck: New tests pass on the fixed code and fail when the tie-break, cut or signature inputs change.
